title: Positive-weight morphism from a commutative algebraic-group torsor
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $H$ be a smooth separated commutative $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], geometrically integral in the sense that it remains nonempty and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] after every field extension. Let $V$ be a $k$-scheme of finite type with a right $H$-action $a:V\times_kH\to V$ (associative and unital). Assume that $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat and surjective and that $(\operatorname{pr}_1,a):V\times_kH\to V\times_kV$ is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $V$ is a torsor under $H$; no $k$-point of $V$ is assumed. There exist a positive integer $n$ and a $k$-scheme morphism $\phi:V\to H$ such that, as morphisms $V\times_kH\to H$,
$$\phi\circ a=m_H\circ(\phi\circ\operatorname{pr}_1,[n]_H\circ\operatorname{pr}_2).$$
Here $m_H$ is the group law and $[n]_H$ is its $n$-fold sum map. Equivalently, for every $k$-scheme $T$ and every $v\in V(T)$ and $h\in H(T)$, $\phi(v+h)=\phi(v)+nh$.

source.place: Lemma 8.22, printed p.152, including its proof: n is 1 for a rational point and otherwise the positive degree of a finite separable residue extension. The equality is an equality of morphisms, not only of rational points.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $f:V\to S$. It is flat and surjective by hypothesis and quasi-compact because it is of finite type. Base change of $H\to S$ along $f$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). The given isomorphism $(\operatorname{pr}_1,a)$ identifies that projection $V\times_kH\to V$ with $V\times_kV\to V$. Thus the base change of $f$ along itself is smooth. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] with $X=Y'=V$, $Y=S$ and $g=f$ to conclude that $V\to S$ is smooth. Smoothness is unchanged by the displayed isomorphism: its local finite presentation and infinitesimal lifting conditions are transported by the inverse, as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Since $f$ is surjective, $V$ is nonempty.

source.place: Lemma 8.22, printed p.152, proof (torsor trivialization, finite separable point and Galois sum); expanded fpqc descent details.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-dense-separable-points], the nonempty smooth $V$ has a closed point $P$ with finite separable residue field $K/k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the one extension $K/k$ to obtain a finite Galois extension $L/k$ and a $k$-embedding $K\to L$. Composing $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ with the residue-field point gives $p\in V(L)$. Here finite Galois means finite-dimensional, separable and normal; no perfectness assumption on $k$ is used.

source.place: Lemma 8.22, printed p.152, proof (torsor trivialization, finite separable point and Galois sum); expanded fpqc descent details.

proof.text: Over any field extension $E/k$ and any $b\in V(E)$, pull the torsor isomorphism back along $b$ in the first $V$ coordinate. This gives the isomorphism $t_b:H_E\to V_E$, $h\mapsto b+h$. Its inverse $d_b:V_E\to H_E$ is a scheme morphism, with $b+d_b(v)=v$ for every $E$-scheme $T$ and $v\in V_E(T)$. Associativity and the uniqueness of this difference give $d_b(v+h)=d_b(v)+h$ on every such $T$. These equations are equations of morphisms: evaluate the formulas on the identity of their source, using the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Lemma 8.22, printed p.152, proof (torsor trivialization, finite separable point and Galois sum); expanded fpqc descent details.

proof.text: Put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Aut}_k(L)$. The finite Galois tensor decomposition [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition](1), followed by [lem-exc-finite-galois-algebra-tensor-decomposition], gives $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_kL)\simeq\coprod_{\sigma\in\Gamma}\operatorname{Spec}L$; on its $\sigma$ component the projections are the identity and $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$. In particular the indexing group is finite; it is nonempty because it contains the identity. Set $n=|\Gamma|>0$. Define the $L$-morphism $F:V_L\to H_L$ by $F=\sum_{\sigma\in\Gamma}d_{\sigma p}$. Here $\sigma p=p\circ\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$, viewed as an $L$-point of $V_L$, and the finite sum uses the multiplication of the commutative group scheme $H_L$. Repeated points in this indexed family are retained. For each $\tau\in\Gamma$, transport along the canonical semilinear $\tau$-actions on $V_L,H_L$ carries $d_b$ to $d_{\tau b}$: apply $\tau$ to $b+d_b(v)=v$ and use uniqueness in the torsor isomorphism. Since $\tau$ permutes the family $(\sigma p)_\sigma$, and addition is commutative, it fixes $F$.

source.place: Lemma 8.22, printed p.152, proof (torsor trivialization, finite separable point and Galois sum); expanded fpqc descent details.

proof.text: The singleton $\operatorname{Spec}L\to S$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: flatness is [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] with $D=k$, both spectra have one point, and the source is affine. On the component labelled by $\tau$ of its double overlap, the compatibility of $F$ with the canonical descent data is precisely its $\tau$-invariance from step 4, because the two projections are the identity and $\operatorname{Spec}\tau$. Hence that compatibility holds on the whole disjoint union. The surjectivity onto compatible morphisms in [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend], with $U=V$ and $W=H$, gives a $k$-morphism $\phi:V\to H$ whose scalar extension is $F$.

source.place: Lemma 8.22, printed p.152, proof (torsor trivialization, finite separable point and Galois sum); expanded fpqc descent details.

proof.text: Step 3 gives, for every $L$-scheme $T$ and $(v,h)\in(V_L\times_LH_L)(T)$, the equality $F(v+h)=\sum_{\sigma}(d_{\sigma p}(v)+h)=F(v)+nh$. The middle equality is finite distributivity in the abelian group $H_L(T)$: by induction, adding the next term adds one more $h$. Thus this is the required equality of $L$-morphisms, by evaluating at the identity of $V_L\times_LH_L$. The map $[n]$ is the repeated-sum group-scheme morphism from [def-sc-group-scheme], and this construction commutes with scalar extension because its structure maps do.

source.place: Lemma 8.22, printed p.152, proof (torsor trivialization, finite separable point and Galois sum); expanded fpqc descent details.

proof.text: Apply the injectivity in [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend] for the same cover, now with $U=V\times_kH$ and $W=H$, to the two $k$-morphisms $\phi\circ a$ and $m_H\circ(\phi\circ\operatorname{pr}_1,[n]_H\circ\operatorname{pr}_2)$. Their base changes agree by step 6, so they agree over $k$. Together with $n>0$ this proves the statement. If $V(k)$ already contains $b$, step 3 itself gives $\phi=d_b$ with $n=1$; the general construction needs no rational point over $k$ and no division by $n$.
